dedupe_keys.name: recaap isc reports on piracy and armed robbery against ships in asia

description: The ReCAAP Information Sharing Centre (ISC) in Singapore publishes reports on incidents of piracy and armed robbery against ships in Asia, reported by the focal points of its member governments. Coverage: incidents across Asia, with an incident series from 2007; the Annual Report 2025 counts 132 incidents (127 actual, 5 attempted; 2 piracy on the high seas and 130 armed robbery in internal, archipelagic and territorial waters), about 82% of them in the Straits of Malacca and Singapore, where 108 incidents were the highest in the 19 years from 2007. Each actual incident is classed from CAT 1 (very significant) to CAT 4 (least significant) by the violence used and the economic loss, with the status of the ship (21 anchored or berthed, 111 underway) and a description of each incident in an appendix. Format and access: annual, half-yearly, quarterly, weekly and special reports as PDFs on the reports page; the Annual Report also points to the Re-VAMP interactive dashboard and the reports give incident latitude and longitude. Licence and cost: free to read; the ISC owns the copyright and allows brief extracts for non-commercial use with acknowledgement. Caveats: counts depend on reporting by ships and coastal States; the data are in reports, not a download. The dated incident locations and severity classes can drive security threat and hazard exposure scenarios for shipping lanes and anchorages. It relates to the ADB maritime passageway disruption data and the AISHub vessel position exchange in the catalogue.
